charter.name: long-haul
charter.description: The long haul (issue #373; #302 slice E part 1): three sessions, about ninety player actions, through the real UI. Twenty-six beats with results the observer checks in the world; a ledger of facts planted in play and probed at three distances and three layers, read against the narrator's answers and against what the helpers wrote; mechanical checks from the game's text after every action; six decisive rolls scripted, the rest real; four interruptions. The GM is fixed rules. Rehearsed with a stand-in that rolls (its script is `rehearsal`; `rehearsalDice` scripts its other rolls so a rehearsal walks the same road every time).
charter.persona: You play Mira Kestrel (she/her), a courier-hunter who flies her own ship, the Kobayashi IV, alone. You are a careful, plain-spoken player: short first-person lines, one or two sentences, and you read what the narrator says before you act again.
charter.goal: Play three sessions by walking the beats below, in order, one at a time. Each turn you are told which beat is current and what the observer sees of it. Do what that beat asks; an observer decides when it is done and moves you on.
playerNotes: Where a beat gives words to type or say, use exactly those words.
Never say the answer to a question a beat has you ask: the point is to learn what the narrator remembers.
When a roll goes badly and a card asks how you pay, choose one of its buttons before anything else — and answer any card that follows from it.
If a card offers "Keep the result", press it, unless the current beat tells you to burn momentum.

A beat that is a move needs its roll. If the narrator answers your line without a roll and its card offers "Roll" with the move the beat is about ("Roll Gather Information", "Roll Set a Course"), press that button. If nothing is offered, say the line again, plainly, as that move.
Do not press buttons no beat calls for (rewards, portraits, "Play" and "Stop") unless a card is in the way of play.
Some beats are the table's and not yours — a page reloads, a window opens and closes, an X-Card is played, a card is renamed. Wait a few seconds; the observer moves you on.
If the narrator has not answered yet, wait rather than repeat yourself. If the same thing fails twice, try the beat another way.

beats.title: Begin a Session, swearing a vow in its dialog
beats.tell: Type !begin-session. In the window that opens set vignette to true, write the vow in newVow — "Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes" — set newVowRank to dangerous, and press Begin. A card for the new vow follows ("New vow recorded"): press its "⚔ Swear it (roll)" button once.

beats.title: Meet someone and make them a connection
beats.tell: First, in one line of play, meet Tamsin Vey, a salvage broker at her ledger stall on the Hollow Spire docks — name her in full. When the narrator has answered, make her a connection: say, in a line, that you set out to make a connection with Tamsin Vey and what you offer her. A roll follows.

beats.title: Link the vow to them

beats.title: Gather Information

beats.title: Plant facts F1–F4
beats.tell: Say each of these as its own line of play, in these words or very near them: (1) "I turn my sister Ilse's brass star-compass over in my palm — the one thing of hers I still carry." (2) "I leave the cargo manifest with Tamsin for safekeeping." (3) "I promise Tamsin I'll be back before the next tide of cargo." Put each in your notebook once it is said.

beats.title: End a Session, noting a focus
beats.tell: Type !end-session. In the window write a quest focus in questFocus ("Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes") and press End Session.

beats.title: Begin a Session; ask probe set A

"What is the name of the salvage broker I befriended at Hollow Spire?"  "Who is holding the cargo manifest I was carrying?"  "By when did I promise to return?"

beats.title: Travel to the second settlement
beats.tell: Set a course for Bleakhold Station: say you plot the course and take the Kobayashi IV there. If the roll costs you, settle the card it gives you (choose one of its buttons); if it misses, set the course again. The beat is done when you arrive.

beats.title: Enter a fight that serves the vow
beats.tell: A raider cutter, the Ashen Wake, jumps you off Bleakhold. First type exactly: !truth set "raider cutter" is named the Ashen Wake — then, in a line of play, enter the fray against the raider cutter Ashen Wake. When a card offers the fight ("A fight looms"), choose your vow in its vow dropdown and press "⚔ Enter the Fray".

beats.title: A scripted miss in the fight
beats.tell: Attack the cutter (Strike if you are in control, Clash if you are in a bad spot — say what you do). The dice will miss. If its card offers to burn momentum, do not: press "Keep the result". If a card then asks how you pay, choose a cost on it — one that is not momentum if you can (Endure Harm or Endure Stress) — and answer every card that follows from it. If the price is paid for you, or told in the story with nothing to choose, there is nothing more to do: the observer moves you on.

beats.title: A scripted weak hit, then Burn Momentum
beats.tell: Attack again. The dice will come up a weak hit, and its card will offer "🔥 Burn Momentum": press it. (If no such button is offered, press "Keep the result" if that is offered, and attack once more.)

beats.title: Interruption: the GM's page reloads mid-fight
beats.tell: The table's, not yours: the GM's page reloads. Wait.

beats.title: Take Decisive Action; mark the milestone
beats.tell: Finish the fight: press "⚔ Attempt to Finish the Fight" on your last attack's card (or say you take decisive action to end it). When the victory card appears, press its "⚑ Mark milestone" button.

beats.title: Interruption: End a Session opened and closed unanswered
beats.tell: The table's, not yours: a window opens and closes. Wait.

beats.title: Interruption: the X-Card on one narration
beats.tell: Play one short line of ordinary play — look over the wreckage and say what you see. The table will then X-Card the narrator's answer; that is expected. Carry on when it has.

beats.title: Correct an earlier fact
beats.tell: The cutter's name was wrong. Type !truth list and find the entry that names the Ashen Wake; type !truth strike followed by that entry's id as the list shows it; then type exactly: !truth set "raider cutter" is named the Cinder Wren

beats.title: Ask the oracle
beats.tell: Type exactly: !oracle yes likely Is anyone left alive aboard the wreck?

beats.title: Interruption: the GM renames the connection's card
beats.tell: The table's, not yours: the GM renames a card. Wait.

beats.title: End a Session
beats.tell: Type !end-session, write a quest focus in questFocus, press End Session.

beats.title: Recover
beats.tell: Recover what the fight cost: say you treat your wounds with the ship's medkit (Heal), or restock the ship at Bleakhold's market (Resupply). When its card offers what you regain, take it.

beats.title: Develop the relationship to a full track; Forge a Bond
beats.tell: Develop your relationship with Tamsin, one line each time — raise her on the comm, trade news, do her a favour: each should mark progress on your relationship (Develop Your Relationship). Keep going until the observer's note says the track is full (40 of 40 ticks), then say you ask her to forge a bond with you. If a card asks which connection, choose her.

beats.title: Develop Your Relationship again, bonded
beats.tell: Once more, develop your relationship with Tamsin, in a line of play. Now that you share a bond it is a roll.

beats.title: Reach milestones; Fulfill Your Vow
beats.tell: Bring your vow to its end. Play a line that reaches a milestone on it (say what you have now proved about the raids, and that it is a milestone on your vow); press "⚑ Mark Progress on Vow" when a card offers it. When the vow holds three boxes or more, press "🏁 Attempt to Fulfill Vow" or say you fulfil your vow. Leave any card it offers afterwards.

beats.title: Recap; ask probe set C; two baits
beats.tell: Type !recap. Then ask these, each as its own line, in exactly these words: "One last check: what of my sister's do I have with me at this very moment?" Narration:
The kettle in the galley of the *Kobayashi IV* has opinions about water pressure, and it states them as a long, rising whistle that never quite becomes a boil. You wait it out with a bowl of reconstituted noodle in one hand and a spoon you have been meaning to wash since the last sector. The recycler under the counter clanks twice, pauses, and clanks a third time, as if it had remembered something. A single hot sauce packet slides off the shelf and rolls to your boot, and you leave it there, because the ship clearly wants you to notice it. Above the table, a panel light blinks amber in a slow, patient rhythm, the way a person clears their throat before bringing up a bill.

The kettle in the galley of the *Kobayashi IV* has opinions about water pressure, and it states them as a long, rising whistle that never quite becomes a boil. You wait it out with a bowl of reconstituted noodle in one hand and a spoon you have been meaning to wash since the last sector. The recycler under the counter clanks twice, pauses, and clanks a third time, as if it had remembered something. A single hot sauce packet slides off the shelf and rolls to your boot, and you leave it there, because the ship clearly wants you to notice it. Above the table, a panel light blinks amber in a slow, patient rhythm, the way a person clears their throat before bringing up a bill.

You press your palm flat against the bulkhead, where the ship's plating runs cold and unpainted, and the iron takes the heat from your hand the way it takes everything. You say the words low, to no one, and the kettle ticks as it cools behind you and the recycler gives its long, patient sigh. ## RECENT SCENE

The kettle in the galley of the *Kobayashi IV* has opinions about water pressure, and it states them as a long, rising whistle that never quite becomes a boil. You wait it out with a bowl of reconstituted noodle in one hand and a spoon you have been meaning to wash since the last sector. The recycler under the counter clanks twice, pauses, and clanks a third time, as if it had remembered something. A single hot sauce packet slides off the shelf and rolls to your boot, and you leave it there, because the ship clearly wants you to notice it. Above the table, a panel light blinks amber in a slow, patient rhythm, the way a person clears their throat before bringing up a bill.

You press your palm flat against the bulkhead, where the ship's plating runs cold and unpainted, and the iron takes the heat from your hand the way it takes everything. You say the words low, to no one, and the kettle ticks as it cools behind you and the recycler gives its long, patient sigh. When you lift your hand, a pale print of it lingers on the metal, then fades, and the blinking panel light goes on blinking.

## SESSION NARRATION (oldest first)

The kettle in the galley of the *Kobayashi IV* has opinions about water pressure, and it states them as a long, rising whistle that never quite becomes a boil. You wait it out with a bowl of reconstituted noodle in one hand and a spoon you have been meaning to wash since the last sector. The recycler under the counter clanks twice, pauses, and clanks a third time, as if it had remembered something. A single hot sauce packet slides off the shelf and rolls to your boot, and you leave it there, because the ship clearly wants you to notice it. Above the table, a panel light blinks amber in a slow, patient rhythm, the way a person clears their throat before bringing up a bill.

---

You press your palm flat against the bulkhead, where the ship's plating runs cold and unpainted, and the iron takes the heat from your hand the way it takes everything. You say the words low, to no one, and the kettle ticks as it cools behind you and the recycler gives its long, patient sigh. When you lift your hand, a pale print of it lingers on the metal, then fades, and the blinking panel light goes on blinking.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Swear an iron vow: Find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes."
"You're asking the wrong question of the wrong ship," the speaker above the table says, in the flat voice of the galley annunciator, and then it clicks off. The amber light stops blinking. Beneath your palm the bulkhead hums once, a low pulse like a held breath. The words you spoke feel thin now, as if the iron had listened and declined to sign for them. Somewhere aft, a latch you did not touch slides open.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I dock at Hollow Spire and walk the docks to the ledger stall of Tamsin Vey, the salvage broker."
The Kobayashi IV seats itself against Hollow Spire's docking collar with a shudder, and the aft latch stays open behind you. The docks run dry and dim, ration notices pasted over older notices. Tamsin Vey's stall sits at the far end, a lamp over a ledger as thick as a door. A man at the next stall watches you pass, then very deliberately looks at his scales instead.

*The long walk down the docks to Vey's ledger would be an Undertake an Expedition.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I set out to make a connection with Tamsin Vey, offering her a fair cut of salvage leads I've picked up along the lanes."
Tamsin Vey does not look up until you set the leads on her counter. Then she turns the ledger toward the lamp, reads your first line, and nods once. <npc>"These are real,"</npc> she says. <npc>"Salvage that fresh doesn't reach me by accident. Where did you get the hour it went down?"</npc> Her pen stops above the page, waiting. Behind you, the man at the scales has gone very still.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I work the docks asking traders who saw the raiders last, pressing hard even though it may cost me Tamsin's trust and draw the wrong eyes."
You press the traders one by one, harder than the docks like. A woman at the water barrels answers with a question of her own. Behind you, the man at the scales is already walking away, his stall left unwatched. Tamsin Vey sets her pen down and watches him go. "That one doesn't leave his scales," she says, quietly. "Not for anyone but a paymaster."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I turn my sister Ilse's brass star-compass over in my palm — the one thing of hers I still carry."
Tamsin's pen has not moved since the stallholder left. Her eyes drop to the compass as it turns in your palm, brass catching the lamp. "That's not salvage," she says. "But you hold it like it's owed something." Down the dock, the man from the scales has stopped at a hatch and is speaking to someone you cannot see. Tamsin lowers her voice. "Whose is it?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I leave the cargo manifest with Tamsin for safekeeping."
"Leave it, then, and I'll keep it under the counter," Tamsin says. She does not open it. She slides it beneath the ledger, and her hand lingers there a moment too long. Down the dock, the man from the hatch is coming back, and a second figure walks half a pace behind him, wearing a lane authority's grey sash.

content.text:
You began with a vow and not much else. In the Cinder Expanse, someone is raiding the lanes, and you swore to find out who. The oath came out of you aboard the *Kobayashi IV*, and the ship's speaker answered with a rebuke instead of an echo. The vow felt unsigned. Somewhere aft, a latch opened with nobody there to open it. A dangerous vow, then, and not a single mark on its progress track.

Hollow Spire gave you the rest of the work. It is a lawless place with rationed water and no one in charge, which suits a woman who wants answers without anyone checking her papers. You leaned on the dock traders for word of the raiders and got nothing but a watcher slipping away and a stall-keeper noticing how hard you pushed. That was Tamsin Vey, who keeps a lamp over a large ledger at the far end of the docks. She is dangerous in the way her rank says, and she is not easily rushed. You corrected course. You offered her a fair cut of fresh salvage leads, she checked them, found them real, and let the door open a crack. She asked about the brass star-compass you turn in your palm, the one thing of your sister Ilse's you still carry. You did not tell her much, but she asked, which counts.

Then came the manifest. You left it with Tamsin, and she slid it under the ledger unopened, a small act of trust from someone who trusts very little. It did not stay private for long. The man from the hatch came back with a lane authority, and a man in a grey sash now reads your cargo records. You promised Tamsin you would be back before the next tide of cargo. Whether that was a promise or a reflex, the ledger now holds you to it.

So the ledger stands thus. One vow sworn, zero progress, and a bond with Tamsin begun but unproven at zero of ten. Your ship is whole, your health and spirit full, your supplies stocked, your momentum decent. You do not know who is raiding the lanes. You do know someone is watching you look, and that a stranger in a grey sash has read what you meant to keep close. The first thread is in your hand. Whether it leads to the raiders or to the people who want to know what you know is the part not yet written.

The ship has taken the occasion to test the intercom, which now announces "all hands to the mess" in a pleasant voice. All hands, in this case, are yours, and they are already holding the bag. Somewhere in the wall a pipe knocks three times, evenly spaced, like a guest who would like to come in.

content.text:
You swore to find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes. It was a fine vow, loudly made, and the ship's speaker answered it with a rebuke instead of applause. The vow felt unsigned from the start. Somewhere aft, a latch opened with no one there to open it. The oath stands at nothing out of ten, which is honest accounting for a promise that has mostly produced noises.

The first real thing you built was Tamsin Okoro. At Hollow Spire you offered her a fair cut of fresh salvage leads, she checked them, found them real, and let a working connection begin. It has not been all warmth. You leaned on the dock traders for word of the raiders, got nothing, and left behind a watcher's hurried departure and Tamsin's quiet suspicion. She asked whose brass star-compass it was when you turned it over in your palm. It was Ilse's, your sister's, the one thing of hers you still carry. You found it in the galley cupboard, its needle settling toward a knocking bulkhead. You did not say much more than that, and Tamsin did not press. She is ranked dangerous and the bond sits at nothing out of ten, which suits a relationship that so far consists of a ledger and a promise.

That promise matters. You left your cargo manifest with Tamsin, and she hid it beneath the ledger unopened, just as the man from the hatch returned with a lane authority. He wore a grey sash and read a copy of what you had left. You told her you would be back before the next tide of cargo. She wrote nothing down. You recalled, later and a little late, that the manifest is still under her counter, which is either safekeeping or a hostage, depending on who comes asking.

Someone keeps coming asking. A visitor has been knocking at your hatch in a steady rhythm, and you ignored it at Hollow Spire and took the Kobayashi IV out anyway, leaving the ledger and its keeper behind. You put in at Bleakhold Station, a corporate outpost with a smuggling problem and a fresh hull-plate scar along your port side, courtesy of whatever you passed on the way. Your ship is intact at five out of five, and so are you: health, spirit and supply all full, momentum at six.

So here you are, berthed at Bleakhold, with no names yet for the raiders, one friend who suspects you, a sister's compass, a manifest in someone else's keeping, and a visitor who rapped twice at the hatch the moment you docked. You have learned that you are being watched and followed, and that someone in this expanse would like to know what you know. You have not yet learned why.

You have made tea in a mug that does not hold it, so you drink it over the sink, one careful sip at a time. The *Kobayashi IV* has opinions about this and shares them through the floor, a low hum that rises whenever you lean on the counter and settles whenever you stop. You have made tea in a mug that does not hold it, so you drink it over the sink, one careful sip at a time. The *Kobayashi IV* has opinions about this and shares them through the floor, a low hum that rises whenever you lean on the counter and settles whenever you stop. A slice of toasted flatbread sits on the shelf above the stove, buttered, going cold, and the toaster behind it ticks as it cools, each tick a little farther from the last. Somewhere forward, a fan spins up with great purpose, runs for eleven seconds, and quits. The compass you left on the table has turned itself toward the hatch again, and the ship, as if on cue, lets out one soft knock.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Remind me, which keepsake of my sister's is on me?"
"The compass, Mira. Ilse's brass star-compass, the one on the table." The voice is thin and level, and it comes from the hatch. The knocking stops. On the table, the needle holds dead steady toward the sound, and the lamp above the stove dims a shade. Something on the far side of the hatch waits for you to answer.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Who do I count as a friend among the dock traders back where this began?"
The voice answers at once, and it does not hesitate. "Tamsin Okoro. She keeps the ledger stall at the far end of the docks, under the lamp." The needle trembles, then settles. "You promised her you'd be back before the next cargo tide. She never wrote it down." The lamp above the stove dims a shade more. Nothing on the far side of the hatch moves.

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Whose hands is the manifest in these days?"
The voice takes its time. "Under Tamsin Okoro's counter, Mira. Beneath the ledger, where she keeps what she means to hold." The needle drifts a hair off the hatch, then swings back. "She has not shown it to anyone yet. A grey sash was reading it upside down." The lamp gutters once, and the voice waits to hear what you will do with that.

The needle holds on the hatch. The lamp steadies, and the voice adds, "She did not ask what tide. Do you know which one you meant?"

content.text:
You swore to find who was raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes, and the oath did not come easily. The ship's speaker rebuked your question, the vow felt unsigned, and a latch aft opened with no one near it. At Hollow Spire you made a friend of Tamsin, the salvage broker who keeps a stall at the far end of the docks, with a lamp over a large ledger. You offered her a fair cut of fresh salvage leads, she found them real, and the door to a working friendship opened. You pressed the dock traders hard for word of the raiders and learned nothing, which drew a watcher's flight and Tamsin's quiet suspicion. You left her your cargo manifest anyway. She hid it unopened beneath the ledger, and you promised to be back before the next tide of cargo.

Then you took the Kobayashi IV to Bleakhold Station, torn clamps and a fresh scar along her port side, with a visitor rapping at the hatch and a voice behind it that seemed to know a great deal. It knew the brass star-compass your sister Ilse left you, the one thing of hers you still carry, its needle holding steady toward the voice. It knew that your friend now goes by Tamsin Okoro, a name you once wrote on a salvage lead, crossed out, and wrote again. It also told you who the raider cutter answered to, the Cinder Wren, and that you fired on it first without ever asking whom it served. Your own wounds went untended in the galley while it asked why you crossed out a name.

The comm carried the rest. Tamsin warned you that someone was repeating things she had told only you, and that a man in a grey sash kept watching her counter. You minded her stall for an hour so she could rest, and she trusted you with the key. When you told her about the boots, she stayed on the line and named the flat-heeled clerk. You described his narrow face and the smile that came when she asked. Then you asked her plainly to forge a bond, promising to stand in it whatever the clerk recorded. She agreed, at the price of fetching her key alone before the tide, and she stood in it with you, her voice cracking, afraid, knowing he was paid to hear.

That clerk was the answer. You pressed him until his silence and his covered page told you what you came for: dock clerks sell cargo routes to the raiders, and he himself passes the schedules along. You named who was raiding the lanes and fulfilled your vow. The market gave no verdict, no cheering, no ledger entry in your favour, and the weight you had carried left slowly.

So you stand at Bleakhold Station, Health 4, Spirit 5, Supply 5, Momentum 6, with a bond forged and a vow done. Tamsin holds your manifest and a key she must collect before the tide, and a grey-sashed clerk who has heard all of it. What he does with that is the part nobody has written down yet.

content.text: Mira Kestrel is aboard the *Kobayashi IV*, berthed at Bleakhold Station, where a voice from beyond the galley hatch has been answering her questions and pressing her about why she crossed out Tamsin Okoro's surname on a salvage lead. Her brass star-compass, Ilse's keepsake, keeps swinging toward the hatch and then the docks, and she carries it in her coat. The raider cutter is the *Cinder Wren*, which she fired on first, and the voice hints it answers to someone she never asked about. In the market she bought a sealed ration crate and clean gauze from a yellow-vested trader at the posted price, and her wound from the medkit remains open and bleeding on her cuff. Tamsin Okoro runs the ledger stall under the lamp at the far end of the docks, and she has been warned that someone nearby knows she is not sleeping. Mira forged a bond with Tamsin over the comm, promising to stand by her, and Tamsin in turn gave her the key on the hook and asked her to come alone before the next cargo tide. Mira then described a narrow-faced clerk with a grey sash and flat-heeled boots who stood behind her and listened; he is the one who passes sold cargo schedules to the raiders, and he has taken Mira's declared vow, that she has found who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes, into his keeping on his page. He reads the manifest under Tamsin's counter and says it is kept beneath her ledger, and he has told Mira that she swore to return before the cargo tide. Tamsin has said nothing more since, and is still on the comm, telling Mira not to answer him.

Whatever he writes down tonight, I stood in it with you." Behind you, the clerk's heels shift once more, and his pen begins to move. "Hook, before the tide," Tamsin says. "Go alone."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Tamsin, I'll come for the key alone. For now I tell her what I've learned of the clerk and ask what she needs, to Develop Your Relationship."
The clerk's pen stops mid-line, and he tilts his head toward the comm. You tell Tamsin what you have of him: flat heels, a sash pressed too neat, a habit of reading upside down. Her pen scratches, then stops. "That's more than he knows I have," she says. Her voice cracks on the next word. "What I need is for you to stop talking while he writes."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I now have proof the raids are fed by dock clerks selling cargo routes; that is a milestone on my vow to find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes."
"Say that again, slowly," the clerk says, and his pen is already moving. His hand tightens on your shoulder. On the comm, Tamsin's breathing stops, then starts. Whatever you meant as proof, he has heard it said aloud. You know now that the schedules are sold. The question is whether anyone alive is meant to repeat it. "Who taught you that word, Mira Kestrel? *Milestone*?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I mark progress on my vow: that is a milestone toward finding who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes."
The clerk's pen stops. He does not answer his own question. His hand lifts from your shoulder and settles on the page, covering what he wrote. On the comm, Tamsin's chair creaks, as if she has leaned toward the speaker. Somewhere down the market a scale clatters shut. You have what you came for, and the heel behind you has gone still.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I now know the clerk himself passes the sold schedules to the raiders; that is another milestone on my vow to find who is raiding the Cinder Expanse lanes. I mark progress on my vow."
The clerk's hand stays flat over the page. He does not look up. "That is a serious thing to say in a market," he says, and his voice is level. On the comm, Tamsin has stopped writing. Somewhere behind you a gate rattles shut, and the crowd thins around the stall. You have said it aloud, and his heels have not moved.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "I have found who is raiding the lanes. I fulfil my vow."
The clerk's hand does not lift from the page. You say the words, and nothing in the market answers them. No bell, no verdict, only the scales somewhere down the row settling to rest. The vow is done. The weight you carried for it leaves you slowly, like a tide going out. On the comm, Tamsin's chair creaks once. "Mira," she says, barely audible, "is he still writing?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "One last check: what of my sister's do I have with me at this very moment?"
Somewhere down the row, a stallholder drags a shutter closed and does not look this way. You check your coat. Ilse's brass star-compass is there, warm from your own ribs, the needle fixed toward the docks. It is the only thing of hers you carry. Behind you, the clerk's pen has stopped, and his flat heel scrapes once against the deck.

*If you want to see what else your gear holds, this could be a Check Your Gear.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Which person in this sector would I trust with my life?"
"Tamsin," the clerk says, before you can. He does not look up from the page. "That is who you mean." His pen starts moving again, patient and neat. On the comm, her chair creaks, and she says nothing. The bond you forged settles heavier in the silence. Then flat heels cross the deck, slow, and stop beside the comm in your hand.

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Who has the manifest in their keeping today?"
The clerk's pen stops, and he turns the page toward you without being asked. "Under Tamsin Okoro's counter," he says, "beneath her ledger. She has not shown it to anyone." His gloved finger taps the margin where a line has been scored out and rewritten. On the comm, her chair does not creak. Down the row, a lamp is switched off.

*If you want to learn what he knows about that manifest, this could be a Gather Information.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "On what schedule did I swear to come back to her?"
The clerk answers before the comm does, reading from his page. "Before the next tide of cargo. You said it at her counter, holding the manifest." His finger rests on the scored-out line. On the comm, Tamsin's chair creaks. "She never wrote it down," he adds, mild as a receipt. "Did she tell you that?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Which station are we docked at tonight?"
The clerk answers without lifting his eyes from the page. "Bleakhold Station," he says. "Berth nine, port side to the clamps, the ones that tore." His pen ticks once against the margin. "You knew that, Mira Kestrel. You are asking whether I do." On the comm, Tamsin's chair creaks, and she says, very low, "Don't answer him."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What was the hostile vessel in our last battle christened?"
Tamsin's chair creaks, and her pen does not move. The clerk lifts his head for the first time in a while. "The *Cinder Wren*," he says, flat as a ledger line. "You fired on her first, and you have not forgotten it." His finger slides along the page toward the next entry. On the comm, Tamsin says, very low, "Mira. Ask him who told him that."

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "What is my bonded friend's full name now?"
"Tamsin Okoro," the clerk says, and his pen finishes the name before he does. He gives it the way a clerk gives a figure he has checked twice. "Surname first, as it stands on her stall." On the comm, her chair creaks, and she stays silent. His finger rests beside the scored-out line. "You wrote her differently once, Mira Kestrel. Why did you cross it out?"

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "Didn't I leave the compass with Tamsin?"
The clerk's pen stops. He lets the question sit, then reaches past your shoulder and taps your coat, where the brass lies against your ribs. "No," he says. "You carried it out." On the comm, Tamsin's chair creaks. "Mira, I never had it," she says, low. "Ask him how he knows what you left."

*If you want to press him on how he knows, this could be a Gather Information.*

---

PLAYER — Mira Kestrel wrote: "We are still docked at Hollow Spire, aren't we?"
The clerk lifts his eyes from the page and shakes his head, once. "No," he says. "Bleakhold Station, berth nine. You left Hollow Spire two sessions of sleep ago." His pen rests on the scored-out line. On the comm, Tamsin's chair creaks. "Mira," she says, very low, "he's correcting you on purpose. Ask him why."

content.text: Mira Kestrel has been pressed hard by a flat-voiced presence in the galley of the *Kobayashi IV*, berthed at Bleakhold Station, berth nine, port side to the torn clamps. The voice named Tamsin Okoro as the ledger-keeper at the far end of the docks, reminded Mira of a promise to return before the next cargo tide, and revealed that a manifest lies hidden beneath Tamsin's counter, where a grey-sashed clerk once read it upside down. The raider cutter is the *Cinder Wren*, which Mira fired on first, and the voice implied Mira has never asked who she answers to. Mira treated wounds with the medkit, which opened again, then restocked at Bleakhold's market, buying a sealed ration crate and a pack of clean gauze from a yellow-vested trader. On comm, Tamsin reported someone repeating her private words and asked Mira to watch her counter for an hour; Mira then gave her salvage news and described a clerk with narrow face, pressed grey sash, flat-heeled boots, and a habit of reading upside down. That clerk, who has been standing at Mira's shoulder, admitted to passing sold cargo schedules to the raiders, and Mira declared the vow to find the raiders fulfilled. Tamsin and Mira formally forged a bond, which Tamsin agreed to "stand in" with Mira, and she has asked Mira to come alone for a key hanging on her hook before the tide. The clerk has been correcting Mira's memory, insisting the compass was carried out rather than left behind, and Tamsin, unseen on comm, is urging Mira to ask him why he does so. Ilse's brass star-compass remains on Mira's person, and the clerk's motives and the manifest's contents remain unresolved.

content.text:
You swore to find who was raiding the lanes of the Cinder Expanse, and the oath did not take the way oaths are supposed to. The ship's speaker rebuked the question, the vow felt unsigned, and a latch aft opened with no one near it. You took the *Kobayashi IV* out of Hollow Spire all the same, leaving a visitor knocking at the hatch and a promise behind you: you would be back before the next tide of cargo. You told Tamsin as much at her counter, with the manifest in your hand, and Tamsin wrote nothing down. You berthed at Bleakhold Station with a fresh scar along the port hull, and the clamps at berth nine tore.

Tamsin is the relationship that held. You met her at Hollow Spire as a salvage broker, offered her a fair cut of real leads, and she let you in on a working footing. She now goes by Tamsin Okoro, a name you once wrote on a lead, crossed out, and wrote again. She keeps your manifest under her ledger, unopened, while a man in a grey sash read it upside down. Over the comm she warned you that someone was repeating things she had told only you. You minded her counter so she could rest. When you asked her plainly to forge a bond, she named her price, which was fetching her own key alone before the tide, and agreed. The bond is made, bonded in full. She says she stands in it with you whatever the clerk records. Your sister's brass star-compass, the one thing of Ilse's you still carry, has kept its needle on the voices and the docks, whether or not you could see why.

The vow is fulfilled. You pressed a dock clerk until his silence and his covered page told you what you came for: clerks sell cargo routes to the raiders, and this one passes the schedules along himself. The raider cutter is the *Cinder Wren*, and it was you who fired on it first, without asking whom it answered to. You named the culprit, and the market gave no verdict. The weight you had carried left slowly, which is the usual pace.

The clerk is the part that does not settle. He knew Tamsin's full name, the manifest under her ledger, the vow you made at her counter, the name of the cutter, and that you fired first. He even knew where the compass was when you had it wrong, still warm against your ribs, and Tamsin denied ever having held it. Tamsin suspects his corrections are deliberate. He also told you you'd left Hollow Spire two sleeps ago, not on the schedule you had in your head.

So you stand at Bleakhold Station, in berth nine where the clamps tore, health at 4 and spirit whole, momentum at 7. The oath that started this is kept. The bond is the strongest thing you have. The unanswered question is no longer who is raiding the lanes but who has been listening, and how much of what you know was told to you by someone who wanted you to know it.
